title: California's 20th Congressional District General Election, 2026
description: California's 20th Congressional District, encompassing parts of Fresno, Kern, Kings, and Tulare counties in the Central Valley, is holding a general election on November 3, 2026. Incumbent Republican Representative Vince Fong, who first won the seat in a 2024 special election to replace former Speaker Kevin McCarthy, is seeking a full term. He faces Democratic challenger Sandra Van Scotter, a disability community advocate and direct support professional. The district is rated as Solidly Republican by the Cook Political Report, reflecting its conservative lean in recent cycles.
polling_note: No public opinion polls specifically for the 2026 general election in California's 20th Congressional District were found. The Cook Political Report rates the race as Solidly Republican.

candidates.name: Vince Fong
candidates.summary: Vince Fong is the incumbent U.S. Representative for California's 20th Congressional District, first elected in a May 2024 special election to succeed Kevin McCarthy. He previously served in the California State Assembly from 2016 to 2024, representing parts of Kern County. Fong focuses on energy independence, agriculture, infrastructure, and supporting military communities at China Lake, Edwards Air Force Base, and Naval Air Station Lemoore.

candidates.name: Sandra Van Scotter
candidates.summary: Sandra Van Scotter is a Democratic candidate running for U.S. House in California's 20th Congressional District. She is a disability community advocate and Direct Support Professional who chairs the Kern Regional Center Self-Determination Program Local Advisory Committee. Van Scotter's campaign priorities include Medicare for All, disability rights, veterans' services, sustainable water policy, and immigration reform.

forecast.rationale: No public district-level polls exist for this race, reducing precision. However, the district is rated Solidly Republican by the Cook Political Report, and incumbent Vince Fong won the seat in 2024 to succeed former Speaker Kevin McCarthy in this historically conservative Central Valley district. The Democratic challenger, Sandra Van Scotter, is a disability advocate and first-time congressional candidate with no indication of strong fundraising or electoral history that would offset the district's partisan lean. Given the strongly Republican district context and no contrary evidence, the race is a Safe Republican hold.
